messages:
Maria G: Quick follow-up from the quant RFC — I sketched a small staging plan for adaptive calibration (per-endpoint shadow + progressive canary). Want feedback on tradeoffs and the rollback triggers.
Alex K: SGTM. Can you call out the perf vs quality checkpoint frequency? That's the main runtime cost.
Maria G: Thinking initial shadow sampling = 2% of traffic, calibration window = 5k tokens, evals every 1 hour. We keep perf telemetry separate (p95/p99) and QA runs on a held prompt set.
Sam T: Ops note: 2% shadow on prod still needs capacity headroom for shadow batching. We should limit shadow route to lower-priority pools.
Jin: Also need explicit guardrail for hallucination regressions. How will we surface quality deltas?
Aria QA: We can compute a small regression score: exact-match for anchors + semantic sim drop for open prompts (embedding cosine). Threshold = delta > 3% exact-match or sim drop > 0.06.
Alex K: That seems reasonable. Runtime cost: computing embeddings for every shadow response is heavy. Suggest we only compute sim for sampled subset (10% of shadow). Rest use lightweight token-level confidence heuristics.
Maria G: Good call. I'll change plan: full-anchor evals on 100% of shadow, semantic sim on 10% sample. Token-confidence heuristic across all shadow requests.
Sam T: For rollout, I propose: shadow -> 1% live canary (read-only) -> 5% canary (read-write with traffic mirroring) -> full. Rollback if any metric crosses guardrails within 2 hours.
Jin: Who owns the canary decision? Product + ML must sign off, ops does rollback. We should document signoff in the runbook.
Maria G: Agreed. Draft runbook snippet: 
```
canary_config:
  stages:
    - shadow: pct=2, metrics=[p95,p99,quality_anchor,semantic_sim], cadence=1h
    - canary_1: pct=1, mode=read-only, cadence=30m
    - canary_5: pct=5, mode=mirror, cadence=15m
  rollback_triggers:
    - p99_latency_increase_pct > 20
    - quality_anchor_drop_pct > 3
    - semantic_sim_drop > 0.06
  owners: ["ML:Maria G","Product:Jin","Ops:Sam T"]
```
Alex K: Nice. One more runtime detail: make the calibration window configurable per-model and expose `calib_mode: incremental | full_recompute`. Incremental is cheaper but can hide slow drift.
Maria G: Yes — default `incremental` for stable models, `full_recompute` for newly onboarded or high-drift workloads. We'll record mode in telemetry.
Aria QA: For QA, we should include focused prompts that exercise extremes (long context, numeric reasoning, creative). I'll add a 50-prompt anchor set per customer tier.
Sam T: Ops: add throttles so shadow traffic never exceeds reserved budget, and a hard kill switch in console.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment started: quant-adaptive-calib v2 -> canary_1 (1%)
Alex K: Keep an eye on KV cache hit rate — switching precision can change cache patterns and skew latency.
Maria G: Good point. We'll surface kv_cache_hit and avg_generation_tokens in dashboards.
Jin: Timeline: shadow this week, canary next Tuesday if no regressions. Product signoff meeting Monday.
Maria G: Thanks all — I'll update the RFC doc and attach the runbook. Anyone want edit rights on runbook? @Aria QA @Alex K @Sam T
Aria QA: Yes please, will add anchor prompts. :white_check_mark:
Alex K: I'll add runtime knobs and the `calib_mode` flag.
Sam T: I'll add ops kill-switch and budget caps.
Maria G: Perfect — tagging this for follow-up on Monday.
